Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the **most inelastic Beer items** in the Dominick's dataset:

---

## 🍺 Most Inelastic Beer Items — Key Findings

### What "Inelastic" Means Here
An elasticity between **0 and -1** means demand barely budges when price rises. The **closer to 0**, the more inelastic — customers keep buying regardless of price changes.

---

| Rank | Item | Elasticity | Interpretation |
|------|------|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | **Miller Lite Beer 12-pk** (9451200) | **-0.11** | Near-zero sensitivity — loyal buyers |
| 2 | **Miller Genuine Draft 12-pk** (9450330) | **-0.14** | Very strong brand lock-in |
| 3 | **Miller Genuine Draft Lt 12-pk** (9450340) | **-0.17** | Consistent demand across price points |

| 8 | **Old Style Light Party Pack** (9408270) | **-0.33** | Similar occasion-driven buying |

---

### 📊 Key Patterns

| Pattern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **Format effect** | **12-packs and party packs** are the most inelastic — bulk buyers are committed purchasers |
| **Brand effect** | **Miller, Budweiser, Coors** — the "Big 3" national brands dominate the inelastic list |
| **Price range** | These items cluster at **$10.99–$11.99** (12-packs) — shoppers accept the price as "normal" |
| **Price CV** | Beer overall has a 47.5% coefficient of variation in price — yet top brands hold demand steady |

---

### 💡 Business Implications

1. **Raise prices on 12-packs of Miller Lite, MGD, and Budweiser** — a +5–8% price increase would lose very few units and likely **grow net revenue**.
2. **Party packs (Old Style, Miller)** are occasion-driven purchases — shoppers are not price-shopping, they're buying for events. These are prime candidates for **margin expansion**.
3. **Avoid deep discounting** on these items — promotions on inelastic items destroy margin without meaningfully lifting volume.
4. **Contrast with elastic items** (longnecks, imports like Heineken/Beck's) where price cuts *do* drive volume — those need a different strategy.

> **Bottom line:** The most inelastic beers are the **mainstream American 12-pack brands**. You can confidently price these up without losing customers.
